citeAs: @misc{kabuye2026ransknow, author = {Kabuye, Henry}, title = {RansKnow: An Open Dataset of Ransomware-Related YouTube Transcripts with MITRE ATT\&CK Annotations}, year = {2026}, publisher = {Kaggle}, url = {https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/henrykabuye/ransknow-v1} }
rai:dataCollection: Videos were identified by keyword-based search (ransomware, extortion, named ransomware families, incident-response terms, etc.; full list in the paper's Appendix A) against 92 curated cybersecurity YouTube channels using the YouTube Data API v3, then filtered for ransomware relevance and technical depth. Transcript text was obtained via official YouTube captions where available, and via local Whisper ASR transcription (OpenAI Whisper, whisper_base) otherwise. All 1128 selected videos and their available transcripts were then passed through the 'Knowledge Agent' (Scripts/knowledge_agent.py), a deterministic regex/keyword-matching pipeline that derives the 37 structured feature columns (ransomware family mentions, MITRE ATT&CK tactic mentions, tool mentions, platform signals) in the released CSVs. No human review, filtering, or correction of individual video selections or extracted features was performed.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web API; Web Scraping; Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: 94 of 1128 video records (8.3%) have no usable transcript text (empty or unavailable), flagged via Transcript_Available=false in each record's *.meta.json; the released feature CSV (Knowledge_Agent_Features_1034.csv) covers only the 1034 records with a transcript. No values were imputed for the missing 94 -- they are simply absent from the feature CSV.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Public YouTube video metadata (title, publish date, duration) via the YouTube Data API v3; official YouTube closed captions where the uploader provided them (Transcript_Provider=youtube_api, 74 videos); audio tracks of the remaining videos, transcribed locally with OpenAI Whisper (Transcript_Provider=whisper_base/local_asr_whisper, 959 videos).
rai:dataImputationProtocol: None. Missing transcripts are represented by absence (see dataCollectionMissingData) rather than imputed content; no structured feature values are imputed -- absence of a mention is encoded as 0/false by the extraction pipeline itself, not inferred after the fact.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Raw transcript text is used as returned by the YouTube API or Whisper, with no manual editing. Structured features are derived by the Knowledge Agent via regex/keyword matching over transcript text and video titles, including an alias-normalization step for ransomware family and tool names. A known failure mode of this alias matching (generic-word alias collisions, e.g. common English words colliding with ransomware family aliases) is audited and quantified in the accompanying paper and in outputs/Family_Alias_Audit.csv.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: 1) Keyword-based video inclusion filtering; 2) transcript acquisition (official captions preferred, Whisper ASR fallback); 3) Knowledge Agent regex/keyword extraction producing the 37 structured columns per video. No tokenization, stopword removal, or other NLP preprocessing is applied to the released transcript text itself -- it is raw ASR/caption output.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No human annotation was performed at any stage. All structured labels (ransomware family, MITRE ATT&CK tactics, tools, platforms) are produced entirely by the automated Knowledge Agent regex/keyword-matching pipeline. This dataset therefore has no independently verified ground truth -- the released labels are weak/pipeline-derived only. This is the central limitation of the dataset and is discussed prominently in the accompanying paper (Section: 'Scope: no independent ground truth').
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Not applicable -- no human annotation platform was used.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Not applicable in the human inter-annotator-agreement sense, since no human annotation was performed. The closest available quality check is a systematic audit of the automated pipeline's alias-matching logic for generic-word collisions (outputs/Family_Alias_Audit.csv), not an annotator agreement study.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Maintained by a single author (Henry Kabuye) on an as-available basis; no fixed release schedule. Updates (e.g. added channels, corrected extraction logic) are tracked as new dataset versions on Kaggle (https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/henrykabuye/ransknow-v1) and as commits to the source pipeline at https://github.com/Henrinnes/RansKnow. Issues can be filed on the GitHub repository.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Geography; Others -- the underlying videos are public YouTube content in which on-screen presenters (security researchers, vendor employees, conference speakers) appear and speak in a professional capacity; video titles and transcripts may name real presenters, companies, and, in some cases, real ransomware victim organizations discussed in public incident reports. No private individuals, and no information beyond what the channels themselves published, is included.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Intended positive impact: supports defensive threat-intelligence research, ransomware trend analysis, and NLP/weak-supervision method development using an openly available corpus, reducing duplicated manual effort to compile such a corpus. Potential negative impact: the same technical detail (tool names, tactics, platforms) that makes the corpus useful for defensive research is, in the source videos, already public and defensively framed -- this dataset does not disclose anything not already public, but aggregating it may modestly ease large-scale automated mining of that information.
rai:dataBiases: Channel-selection bias: the 92 channels are a curated, primarily English-language, Western/US-UK-centric set of professional cybersecurity vendors, conferences, and creators -- not a representative sample of all ransomware discourse. Keyword-inclusion bias: only videos matching a fixed keyword list are included. Extraction bias: structured labels reflect the Knowledge Agent's regex/keyword coverage, including known generic-word alias collisions (see dataAnnotationAnalysis). Transcription bias: ASR-derived transcripts (93% of records) are less reliable on unfamiliar technical jargon (e.g. malware family names) than official captions, as quantified in the accompanying paper's perturbation-robustness analysis.
rai:dataLimitations: This dataset has no independent, human-verified ground truth: all structured labels are produced by an automated regex/keyword pipeline, not verified by human annotators. It should not be used to make claims about the true real-world accuracy of ransomware family, tactic, tool, or platform classification. It is appropriate for weak-supervision research, label-noise-robust method development, and exploratory NLP/threat-intel text mining, where the labels are treated as pipeline-agreement targets rather than verified truth. 94 of 1128 records lack transcript text. Coverage is skewed toward English-language, Western security-vendor content.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 0 -- no human annotators were used; every label is produced once, deterministically, by the automated Knowledge Agent pipeline (see dataAnnotationProtocol).
rai:annotatorDemographics: Not applicable -- no human annotators were used.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Custom Python regex/keyword-matching pipeline ('Knowledge Agent', Scripts/knowledge_agent.py); YouTube Data API v3 for video metadata and official captions; OpenAI Whisper (whisper_base, run locally) for ASR fallback transcription.

description:
# RansKnow: Ransomware Knowledge Dataset

A curated dataset of **1128 video records** (1034 with full transcripts) sourced from **92 cybersecurity YouTube channels**, built to support knowledge extraction, NLP research, and threat intelligence analysis focused on ransomware.

---

## Background

Ransomware attacks are one of the most damaging categories of cyber threats, yet knowledge about tactics, tools, and affected platforms is scattered across conference talks, incident response reports, and security briefings. RansKnow systematically collects and structures this knowledge from publicly available video content.

Videos were selected using keyword-based inclusion criteria (ransomware-relevant terms), filtered for technical depth, and processed through a Knowledge Agent pipeline to extract structured features aligned with the MITRE ATT&CK framework.

---

## Repository Structure

```

├── transcripts/                  # 1128 video records across 92 channels
│   ├── C01_The_DFIR_Report/
│   │   ├── V0001.txt             # Raw transcript (YouTube timestamped format)
│   │   ├── V0001.meta.json       # Video metadata
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── C02_SANS_Digital_Forensics_and_Incident_Response/
│   └── ... (C01–C101, with gaps for channels excluded after review)
│
├── outputs/                      # Knowledge Agent extraction results
│   ├── Knowledge_Agent_Features_307.csv
│   ├── Knowledge_Agent_Features_307.xlsx
│   ├── Knowledge_Agent_Output.csv
│   └── Knowledge_Agent_Uncertainty_Distribution.png
│
├── RansKnow_v1/

│
├── Scripts/                      # Data pipeline notebooks and scripts

├── Ransomware_Transcript_Dataset_Summary.pdf
└── Video_Selection_Rubric_AutoScore_Filled_6.xlsx
```

---

## Knowledge Agent Feature Schema

All 1034 videos with real transcripts have been processed through the Knowledge Agent pipeline (`Scripts/knowledge_agent.py`), producing **37 structured feature columns** (see `outputs/Knowledge_Agent_Features_1034.csv`):

| Category | Columns |
|---|---|
| **Identifiers** | `Video_ID`, `Channel_ID`, `Channel_Name`, `Video_Title`, `YouTube_URL`, `Transcript_Path` |
| **Ransomware Families** | `Family_Count`, `Family_List` |
| **MITRE ATT&CK Tactics** | `Tactic_Initial_Access`, `Tactic_Execution`, `Tactic_Persistence`, `Tactic_Privilege_Escalation`, `Tactic_Credential_Access`, `Tactic_Lateral_Movement`, `Tactic_Discovery`, `Tactic_Command_and_Control`, `Tactic_Exfiltration`, `Tactic_Impact`, `Tactic_Total_Mentions`, `Dominant_Tactic` |
| **Tools** | `Tool_Cobalt_Strike`, `Tool_Mimikatz`, `Tool_PsExec`, `Tool_Rclone`, `Tool_MegaNZ`, `Tool_AnyDesk`, `Tool_TeamViewer`, `Tool_BloodHound`, `Tool_Total_Mentions`, `Tool_List` |
| **Platforms** | `Platform_Signal`, `Platform_Windows`, `Platform_Linux`, `Platform_ESXi` |

## Transcript Format

Each `.txt` file contains the raw YouTube transcript in timestamped format:

```
0:00
Welcome to the DFIR report...
0:05
Today we are covering a LockBit intrusion...
```

Each `.meta.json` file contains structured metadata:

```json
{
  "Video_ID": "V0001",
  "Channel_ID": "C01",
  "Channel_Name": "The DFIR Report",
  "Channel_UC": "UC6R2MPMkkCqFxvAdQAI_23A",
  "YouTube_Video_ID": "xxxxxx",
  "Video_Title": "...",
  "Year": 2024,
  "PublishedAt": "2024-03-15T14:00:00Z",
  "DurationSeconds": 1843,
  "DurationISO": "PT30M43S",
  "Matched_Keywords": "ransomware;ir",
  "Transcript_Available": true
}
```

---

## Intended Use Cases

- Ransomware threat intelligence research
- NLP and information extraction on cybersecurity text
- MITRE ATT&CK tactic classification
- Tool and platform attribution modelling
- Knowledge graph construction for ransomware
- Curriculum development for cybersecurity education

---

## Dataset on Kaggle

The full dataset (including transcript zips, scripts, and rubrics) is also available on Kaggle:
[https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/henrykabuye/ransknow-v1](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/henrykabuye/ransknow-v1)

---
